messages:
maya: heads-up — thinking about exposing per-route telemetry in the console: sample-rate, redact-level, and whether a request hit a fallback route due to quota. want to align before i mock UI.
jon: curious what you mean by redact-level. are we talking full deid vs hashed vs keep? :thinking_face:
maya: yep. three knobs: none, hash-only, deid. plus an inspect-mode that allows unredacted replay for SRE with breakglass.
ashley: product question: if we surface fallback routing (e.g. routed to cheaper model / region) users might misinterpret it as degraded quality. need clear labels and a reason code.
samir: from infra side, we already attach route metadata: {route_id, model_variant, quota_bucket, sample_key}. exposing those is fine but we must avoid leaking raw request content in the UI.
jon: main privacy constraints:
- UI must never show unredacted user PII by default.
- breakglass must be audited + ephemeral tokens + explicit justification.
- retention for unredacted captures should be short (7 days?) and stored encrypted with KMS.
maya: proposed console UX flow:
1) per-route row shows sample-rate + redact-level + last-fallback-reason (if any)
2) clicking into a route opens Telemetry > Samples where you can view sampled request/response with redaction applied
3) an 'inspect' toggle for on-call that requests a short-lived unredacted token. requires justification text and automatic audit entry.
ashley: ok but we need to think about quotas: if inspect shows unredacted payload from a high-volume tenant, we should rate-limit those inspect queries. also product wants ability to opt routes into more/less sampling so users can increase visibility during rollout.
jon: also want to ensure sampling rules are deterministic for a route so we don't bias by user. we should key sampling on hashed customer_id + route_id so sample-rate is stable per-customer.
samir: agree. sample config like:
```
routes:
  - id: "nlp-chat"
    sample_rate: 0.01
    sample_key: "cust_id:route_id"
    redact_level: "hash"
    allow_inspect: true
    inspect_ttl_seconds: 600
```
maya: question: when redact_level = "hash" do we store both hashed PII and deidentified tokens? i.e., do we keep a salted hash + sketch of entity types so downstream evals can group by entity without seeing raw data?
jon: yes store salted hashes and entity-type annotations (PERSON, EMAIL, CC#) but no raw tokens. the salt must be per-customer or per-org to prevent cross-tenant linking.
ashley: product also wants to show sample coverage stat (percent of unique users seen in samples vs total). that requires mapping sample_key back to user counts — hashed is fine as long as counts are deterministic.
maya: another edge: fallback routing for quota (we fall back from gpt-x to gpt-x-small). Should that be considered a privacy-affecting event? we might log reason: "quota-fallback" which is a safe string.
samir: logging plan: attach event labels only (e.g., fallback_reason:"quota-fallback"), don't attach decision traces that contain internal thresholds to avoid exposing implementation.
jon: audit-bot note: any unredacted inspect must produce an audit event with fields: who, justification, route_id, sample_id, start_ts, end_ts, token_id. audit-bot will post the event and keep a copy in the audit ledger.
audit-bot: auto: audit entry created for inspect attempts will be immutable and searchable by security and compliance teams.
ashley: UX ask: make the inspect rationale free text but add structured checkboxes: production-incident / customer-request / regression-debug. that will help compliance filtering.
maya: rollout plan: toggle per-org in Console > Feature Flags. default off for all orgs. gradually enable for internal teams, then Trusted Partners. no public rollout until product + sec signoff.
jon: operational constraints: breakglass tokens must auto-expire and be revoked on user deprovision. retention of unredacted artefacts: 7 days max and immutable audit record for 7 years.
samir: we also need a safe scrub pipeline for logs exported to third-party analytics: before export apply the same redact_level per-route.
maya: final ask — can eng-platform review a quick RFC on config grammar + inspect flow? i'll draft and ping #eng-security for policy alignment.
ashley: +1 from product. please include sample UI mock (tiny table) and copy for the tooltip explaining fallback.
jon: will review the RFC for privacy requirements.
samir: will add infra constraints (kms, token lifecycle). happy to pair.
maya: thanks team — i'll put the RFC up by EOD.
